items.fact: Which side of the summit block the route climbs (south/west vs east/northeast)
items.prior_evidence: STRUCTURAL: clear pitch_detail (its four rows are the 2004 Overcoat/Chimney-saddle line: col, loose south ridge, west-side ledge traverse, summit block) and replace climbing_route[1] ('Heathery slot to the notch', stepping out left/west) and climbing_route[2] ('Angled chimney to the saddle') with the east-face steps (leave the snow finger at the dark towers, round the corner east, steep gully on solid holds to the summit), keeping the south-ridge line only as a named alternative in approach_variants. The east line is the most documented one in current use: the club route page says to contour from camp east to a notch on Overcoat's north ridge, reach the upper glacier, find a snow finger from the glacier to the east face and climb Class 3 ledges to the summit; a 2024 three-day report climbed the snow finger, moved onto rock near the dark towers, rounded the corner east and went up a steep gully, descending east by heather ledges, a dihedral and two rappels; the only climbing-database listing is 'East Face'. Only the 2004 report takes the south ridge. The row's waypoints, climbing_route[0] and [3], descent_text, rappels and the approach baseFinding already describe the east line, so the replacement is a line clear plus new pitch rows, which the patch format cannot express.

items.fact: Approach-day (day 1) duration vs its own schedule
items.prior_evidence: The club route page gives about 2 hours of biking to the old trailhead and 3-4 hours on to Overcoat Lake (roughly 5-6 hours), but the row's day 1 ends higher, at the benches above the glacier (~6,600 ft), and the 2024 report that follows this itinerary gives no clock times. Neither source supports the 12 h schedule or the 9 h figure for reaching the glacier camp, so nothing is changed.

items.fact: dist_km vs one-way and round-trip distance figures elsewhere
items.prior_evidence: No source states a one-way trailhead-to-summit distance. The club route page gives 10 miles of biking or hiking to about a mile before the old Dutch Miller Gap trailhead, then a ford and steep forest to Overcoat Lake without a mileage; the 2024 report gives 40.4 mi round trip for a loop with extras and Camp Pedro at mile 13. The two do not even agree where the ford falls, and any one-way figure would have to be assembled from pieces, so dist_km (32.5 km) is left as is.

items.fact: Waypoint mileages vs the approach text's mileages
items.prior_evidence: A second mileage-bearing source now exists but disagrees with the first: the club route page puts the river crossing about 10 miles in (a mile short of the old Dutch Miller Gap trailhead), which fits the Overcoat Lake waypoint's 'roughly 10 mi in' note, while the 2024 report puts Camp Pedro, before the ford, at mile 13, which fits the approach text's 13-14 miles. The sources split, so neither the waypoints nor the approach text is changed.

items.fact: 'Base of west ridge' waypoint (6,800 ft, 5.2 mi) sits before the 7,100 ft camp although the ridge scrambling starts at the ~8,000 ft col above camp
items.prior_evidence: STRUCTURAL: the 'Base of west ridge' pin (6,800 ft, distMi 5.2, coordinate 47.5575,-120.842 where the ground is ~7,308 ft) should be MOVED to the ~8,000 ft saddle between Windy Ridge and Cashmere where the ridge scramble starts (and re-elevated to ~8,000 ft with a distMi beyond the 6.5 mi camp), or else renamed as the leave-trail point (~6,700-6,900 ft, on the Windy Pass trail above Lake Caroline) and moved there. Sources: a scramble write-up says leave the Windy Pass trail at 6,700 ft, angle up to the 8,000 ft level and run the ridge to the prominent 8,000 ft saddle; a 2018 report left the trail near a ~6,900 ft meadow and reached the saddle at 8,000 ft; a 2016 report camped in Windy Basin at 6,500 ft and gained the ridge at the low saddle between Windy Ridge and Cashmere. Either fix needs a pin move, which the patch format cannot express; no text patch.

items.fact: Recommended start time from high camp — 5:00 AM vs ~6:00 AM
items.prior_evidence: No source states a recommended departure from the high camp: a 2016 party camped in Windy Basin reached the summit 4.4 hours from camp shortly before noon (a start near 7:30-8 AM), and a 2018 party rose after 8 AM from a Lake Caroline camp; other reports are single-day pushes from the trailhead. Neither 5:00 AM nor ~06:00 is supported, and a start recommendation is a planning choice rather than a researchable fact, so nothing is patched.

items.fact: Pitch count
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. Sources still split by convention over one physical line: the route listing (posted by a first-ascent party member) gives 5 pitches with P5 a ~100 m simul-climbed 4th/low-5th finish; the encyclopedia's route table and a crag database both list 4 pitches (likely not independent of each other); a 2015 trip report describes four belayed pitches then simul-climbing to the summit, consistent with either count. The row is split the same way (pitches, beta, turnaround, pro_tips and watch_out use a P5; overview, descent_text, itinerary and pitch_detail say four), so adopting either number means rewriting four or five fields on a convention call rather than a settled fact. No patch.

items.fact: Pitch 3 and 4 lengths: pitch_detail 35 m / 40 m vs beta ~60 m / ~45 m
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. The route listing (first-ascent party) gives ~30, ~30, ~60, ~45 m and ~100 m for the finish; beta and pro_tips ('the 60 m P3') follow it, and length_m 265 equals that sum, so three row fields plus one source favour 60/45 over pitch_detail's 35/40. No second source gives pitch lengths (the encyclopedia table, the crag database and the 2015 trip report give none), and three fields fall short of the 4-field bar for an internal fix, so no patch.

items.fact: Round-trip distance
items.prior_evidence: dist_km 7.2 (4.5 mi) equals the trail distance to Lake Ingalls alone (9.0 mi round trip), and the wall lies beyond the lake over the meadows toward Stuart Pass, so the stored figure is almost certainly short of the true one-way approach. But only one source gives a mileage on this line and none states the distance to the West Face Wall itself, so the value is left for a second source rather than cleared on inference.

items.fact: Commitment grade (commitment III vs beta 'Grade: IV')
items.prior_evidence: The only numeral published for this route is IV (IV 5.11+) in the first-ascent party's journal note; the route database page, shared by the same first ascensionist, gives no commitment numeral, and no independent account grades it. One source, so commitment III and the beta's IV are left as they are.

items.fact: Total elevation loss for the trip
items.prior_evidence: A third search turned up no car-to-car gain or loss for Sheep Gap's main summit: results are Gothic Basin hikes (about 10.5 mi and 3,700 ft to the basin), Gothic/Del Campo outings and the 2024 North/Middle peak recon, all different objectives. The peak database that would hold ascent GPS logs returned 403 directly. loss_ft 3452 is the net relief, not a cumulative figure, but setting it equal to gain by out-and-back reasoning is refused as a class. No patch.

items.fact: Round-trip mileage
items.prior_evidence: No new measured round trip for the main summit. Gothic Basin alone is described as ~10.5 mi round trip, which makes the itinerary's 11.8 mi for a route that continues ~1.4 mi past the basin to Weden Pass and the summit look short, and the only measured outing to the neighbouring North/Middle peaks logged 13.8 mi, leaning toward partner_requirements' 13-14 mi. But no source states the main-summit figure, and a total assembled from the basin figure plus a leg would be computed. No patch.

items.fact: dist_km (4.5 km) is the camp-to-Austera leg, not the one-way approach
items.prior_evidence: New figures this pass are all per-leg or multi-peak: a club route profile gives trailhead to Klawatti Col 7-9 hr / 5,600 ft and col to Austera 2 hr / 530 ft (no miles); a winter trip gives 16 mi / 9,000 ft for Klawatti plus Austera together. No source states a one-way trailhead-to-Austera distance and dist_km may not be assembled or halved from a multi-peak round trip, so it stays.

items.fact: Total route gain/distance vs. approach-to-camp leg only (dist_km 11.3)
items.prior_evidence: dist_km 11.3 km (7 mi) is the trailhead-to-camp leg in the row's own approach text, not trailhead-to-Austera, but it is longer than the 8.5 km straight line between trailhead and summit, so it is not provably wrong as a one-way figure, and no two sources state a one-way distance to Austera (the only whole-trip figure, 19 mi round trip, is a three-peak outing). Left for a sourced value.

items.fact: Aspect/face of the documented Walrus Glacier line
items.prior_evidence: STRUCTURAL: the row is two lines under one name and needs splitting (or a rename plus a climbing_route rewrite), which the patch format cannot express. Sources agree Clark has two standard ways up: a glacier route on the northeast/east side (the Walrus/Clark Glacier) and a non-glacier scramble on the south-west side that crosses the ridge south of Pt. 8373 by one improbable gully and finishes on Clark's southwest/west ridge. The row's aspect W, face 'West Ridge' and climbing_route[] (Pt. 8373 gully, final south/west ridge) all describe the scramble, while beta describes the Walrus Glacier and says the glacier-free line 'is not the line documented here'. Proposed: either split into a 'Southwest Ridge' scramble row (aspect W/SW, keep climbing_route) and a 'Walrus Glacier' row (aspect NE/E, keep beta), or rename this row to the scramble and rewrite beta to it with the glacier kept as an approach_variants alternative. Sources: a winter ascent report naming the two main routes (glaciated NE slopes vs SW scramble via the gully by Pt. 8373 and the SW ridge) and a 2017 report finishing the scramble on the west ridge.

items.fact: Pitch count
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. A crag database lists Scarface as 6 pitches, Grade III, 366 m (the row's pitches=6 and length_m=366 match it exactly, so they probably came from it). The archived first-ascent trip report (read in full this time) names the 2nd, 3rd and 4th pitches and 'the last couple moderate pitches' but gives the count only on a topo image; the route listing says P5+ without a number. One source for 6 and none for 5, so neither pitches nor the itinerary's '5 pitches' is changed.

items.fact: Rope length
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. More Triple Couloirs accounts again report what individual parties used rather than a required length: a 2018 party roped up for the WI2+ ice and simul-climbed an ~80 m pitch to a rappel anchor, a 2015 party pitched out the runnels in full rope lengths without stating the rope, and the earlier accounts split between a 30 m rope and a thin 6 mm 60 m rope. None addresses rope length for the Hidden Couloir entry gully that this row covers, and the row's own corrections call the 30 m an estimate, so neither the gear list's 60 m nor rope_length_m 30 is adopted.

items.fact: Trailhead waypoint (4,700 ft) sits higher than the crag base (4,601 ft) although the approach hikes uphill to the crag
items.prior_evidence: Same shared East Face waypoints as wa_project_crack. No source states the parking elevation; OpenStreetMap shows two candidate parking spots (USGS ground ~4,741 ft at a layby 0.3 mi from the cliff, ~4,429 ft at an unpaved lot 0.9 mi away) and no source says which is used. USGS ground at the mapped cliff is ~4,783 ft, which also questions the crag waypoint's 4,601 ft. Needs one pin-and-elevation rework across the East Face rows; not patched.

items.fact: Elevation gain for the route
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. The live row no longer carries the crag waypoint (only the Alpental lot, with no elevation, and Guye's summit at 5,168 ft), and gain_ft is still 1,200. The route's database page says only that the crag is isolated from the rest of Guye, near the base of the South Rib, just around the corner right of and below the west face, and visible from the west-most Summit West lots; it gives a 50 ft single pitch and no approach time or elevation. OpenStreetMap maps no climbing feature on Guye Peak. A crag 'down low' near the base of the rib, a half-mile walk from a ~3,127 ft lot, makes 1,200 ft look high, but no source states the crag's height or the walk's gain, so gain_ft is neither replaced nor nulled.

items.fact: Permit field names the Wild Sky Wilderness
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. Re-measured with the Forest Service wilderness boundary layer (with geometry): the crag pin lies OUTSIDE any wilderness, 165 m south of the Henry M. Jackson Wilderness boundary, and the ground height at the pin (4,758 ft, USGS 1 m DEM) fits the approach described for the crag (about 1,000 ft of gain from the hairpin pulloff), while the boundary point 165 m north is already at ~5,230 ft. Wild Sky Wilderness is more than 4 km away, so the Wild Sky name is certainly wrong. But no source states the crag's wilderness status or permit rule, and a 165 m margin is within the uncertainty of a guidebook-database pin, so the replacement text (no permit vs. a Henry M. Jackson self-issue permit) is still not settled; nothing patched. Suggested owner fix: drop the Wild Sky clause from `permit` so it agrees with access.permit 'N/A'.

items.fact: First ascent of Klawatti Peak
items.prior_evidence: Third pass, now with the primary record: the 1940 club annual reports that Lloyd Anderson, Tom Gorton and a guest, Carl Boyer, climbed 'Sloppy Mountain' (Klawatti) and Dorado Needle on July 7, 1940, and says fuller accounts were kept in the climbing committee's files — it names no route or face. The long-form peak page (archived) repeats the party and date without a route; the only source tying the 1940 party to the SW Buttress is still the one route database. Party and date are confirmed for the peak; which line they climbed is not, so the row's fa (credited to this route) is left.

items.fact: Which side of the peak the route climbs from the gap (east ridge/face vs southwest slopes 'staying left of the broad west ridge')
items.prior_evidence: STRUCTURAL: rename the route from 'Southwest Slopes' to an East Ridge name, and rewrite approach (last sentences), climbing_route[0] (label and notes), approach_variants[0].baseFinding (last paragraph), descent_text (first sentences), beta and the La Bohn Gap / summit waypoint notes so they describe ascending the ridge west from the gap onto the peak's east side, as descent, itinerary day 2 and its schedule already do. Sources: the peak's encyclopedia entry places La Bohn Peak west of La Bohn Gap and names the East Ridge (class 2) as the easiest route; a 2021 report reaching the gap from Chain Lakes turns left at the gap up boulders onto the ridge, then a narrow ridge to the summit block with a cliff on the north side, matching the east-ridge wording (not a southwest-slopes line). No source describes a southwest-slopes line from the gap. The rename cannot be expressed as a patch.

items.fact: round-trip distance and gain figures disagree
items.prior_evidence: Third attempt. New figures found add to the spread rather than converging: a 2025 party recorded 5.71 mi and 4,122 ft round trip and another report calls it more like 6.2 mi, alongside the earlier 4.62, 5.3, 7.0, 7.4 and 8.0 mi. No two independent sources state the same distance or gain for this path.

items.fact: Distance up the Chiwawa River Trail to the Massie Lake turnoff: approach/itinerary/sectionBreakdown 'about 4 miles' vs the 'M' tree waypoint distMi 2.8 (and lake 4.7)
items.prior_evidence: Third attempt. Figures for the Trinity-to-turnoff distance still do not converge: one high-route description says roughly 4 miles, a different party approx 3-4 miles, a summary cites about 3 miles, and a 2005 party describes a 1.4 mi leg plus a 3.1 mi leg before the lake path with the lake path itself 1.4 mi (another says ~2 mi). OpenStreetMap puts Massie Lake about 4.6 mi in a straight line from Trinity, which makes the lake pin's distMi 4.7 implausibly short for a trail-plus-sheep-path route, but no two sources state the same cumulative figure for either pin, and new distMi values would have to be computed, so nothing is changed.

items.fact: Crux grade shown in TECHNICAL STATS vs actual crux difficulty
items.prior_evidence: Still real: grade 'Class 4' vs rock_grade '5.0 (crux dihedral...)', and the row itself splits on whether the 5.0 dihedral is on the standard east-ridge line or a SE-face variant. Third pass: peak database pages are behind a bot wall (archive copy holds no route data), the photo pages found carry no rating, and the encyclopedia entry and a spring snow ascent give no rock grade. Still only one ascent rates the line, so nothing is changed.

items.fact: total elevation gain/loss
items.prior_evidence: Still real: gain_ft/loss_ft 10,700 vs itinerary days 7,500 up / 8,900 down. Published figures for the Bridge Creek approach still split (37 mi / 8,400 ft on the hiking-guide/club page and a trip report derived from it; 38.3 mi / 10,700 ft on a speed-record route page; 11,000+ ft on a 2025 single-day ascent); 10,700 and 11,000+ are not the same stated figure. No new independent source found; balancing the itinerary days would require computing.

items.fact: Bergschrund/glacier hazard on a rock-route approach that has no glacier
items.prior_evidence: watch_out still lists a bergschrund crossing at the base. Third pass: route pages describe the wall as rising from the snow between Stuart Pass and Goat Pass, reached from near the toe of the West Ridge, with no moat or bergschrund named; the only moat mentions found concern other Stuart routes or other ranges. No source confirms or rules out a schrund at this base, so the line is neither removed nor confirmed.

items.fact: Crux/route grade (Class 4, 5.0) vs. the pitch-by-pitch breakdown's max grade (Class 3)
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. The only other account reached, a WTA trip report of the same July 2023 north-ridge ascent, is by the same author as the blog already tried (it lists only a helmet as gear and gives no class), so it counts as the same source. Searches for a peak-log entry, an older journal note or a second party's report on the Swamp Creek north ridge found nothing that grades the 7,300-7,400 ft crux. The row still says Class 4 (5.0 crux) in grade, Class 3-4 in the itinerary and Class 3 at most in pitch_detail, and no two sources settle which is right.

items.fact: Total round-trip distance for the Standard Route
items.prior_evidence: Still no source that states the trailhead-to-Sentinel one-way or round-trip distance for this route alone: a 2024 out-and-back Ptarmigan party logged per-day totals only (16.5/14.1/11.0/9.4 mi, including a 3 mi gated road walk and the traverse to Dome), and search summaries repeat the single 32.6 mi Sentinel + Old Guard round trip that includes road walk, Old Guard and a camp move. A notable coincidence: dist_km 26.2 equals, as a number, the 26.2 MILE round trip the same author gives for Le Conte Mountain from the Cascade Pass trailhead, which suggests dist_km was carried from a different objective and unit, but that is not a stated figure for this route. Waypoints (summit at 14 mi) and the itinerary (34.1 mi incl. Old Guard) still cannot be reconciled from two sources; no patch.

items.fact: Sherpa south basin camp waypoint elev 6200 vs elevFt 6300
items.prior_evidence: Unchanged: waypoints[2] stores elev 6200 and elevFt 6300; bivy[0] of the same name says 6200. The waypoint has no coordinate, so no ground height can be read, and neither this pass nor earlier ones found a published elevation for this informal camp (route write-ups give Longs Pass ~6,200 ft and a basin camp 'around 6,800 ft' on the neighbouring East Ridge row, which is a different spot or a different estimate). The rendered waypoint list shows elev (6200), agreeing with the bivy, so the visible page is consistent; only the non-rendered elevFt differs. No patch without an external figure.

items.fact: Where the climbers' path leaves the maintained trail (Park Creek Pass traverse vs the ~4,100 ft washout on the Park Creek trail)
items.prior_evidence: STRUCTURAL: two sources now state the low start explicitly and neither describes a traverse from the pass. The peak's route page: from Park Creek Camp (2,280 ft) follow the Park Creek trail ~2 mi to a creek-crossing camp, then ~2 mi more to a large washout/rockslide of whitish rock; the boot path to Storm King (and Goode) starts about five minutes up-trail beyond it, marked by a small cairn; the Thunder Creek approach crosses Park Creek Pass, descends into Park Creek and climbs back up southeast then east. The club route page: from Two Mile Camp (3,400 ft) ascend ~2 mi to ~4,100 ft, cross a large washout, look for a small cairn a few hundred yards on and climb the burned ridge, trending climber's left through heather and game trails to cairned Class 2-3 ground and the basin below Goode at 7,400 ft. The row's own coordinates also put the peak and the rib camp EAST of the pass, not west. What should change: approach (sentence 'From Park Creek Pass, leave the maintained trail and traverse cross-country west/southwest ... roughly a mile to reach the cirque'), approach_variants[0].notes (same paragraph), waypoints[3].directions ('Leave the maintained trail at the pass and traverse ... west/southwest') and descent_text ('reverse the cross-country traverse east back to Park Creek Pass') should describe crossing the pass, descending the Park Creek trail to the ~4,100 ft washout and climbing the ridge to the 7,400 ft basin (matching itinerary day 2 and timing.sectionBreakdown[1]); the waypoint list needs a washout/boot-path junction pin and the rib camp's distMi (21, only 1.4 mi past the pass) re-measured, which needs a pin addition and distances no source states. That exceeds the patch format, so no patch.

items.fact: Whether a wilderness permit is needed
items.prior_evidence: The Barclay Lake Trailhead page lists only recreation-pass/day-use fee payment (Northwest Forest Pass, Interagency, scan-and-pay) and no wilderness permit; an archived Barclay Lake hike page lists only a Northwest Forest Pass. The forest-wide wilderness page still says only that day-use visitors 'may need' a free self-issue permit, without naming Wild Sky. No source states either that Wild Sky uses a self-issue permit or that it does not, so neither the permit column nor access.permit can be confirmed.

items.fact: How long consolidated/climbable snow lasts on the route
items.prior_evidence: No new source gives a snow window; the known accounts are a June 2020 party that met an unusually large snowpack and a November 2025 party with thin snow over class 4 rock. The season column holds a sentence owned by another session, so nothing is edited.

cleared_value.notes: From the base of the gully, class 2-3 talus and loose scree — rockfall is a real concern with any party above you.

cleared_value.label: Narrow class 4 step
cleared_value.notes: Roughly midway up, the gully narrows to a steeper class 4 step of cleaner rock.

cleared_value.label: Scramble to the belay ledge
cleared_value.notes: Above the step, scrambling leads to a flat belay ledge about 200 ft below the true summit, where the final short technical section begins.
Cross or circle the Overcoat Glacier from high camp to the notch/col between Chimney Rock and Overcoat Peak; rope and crampons typically used.
Shed glacier gear at the col and step directly onto the south ridge; rock is loose for roughly the first 20 feet.
A ledge traverses the west side of the south ridge with real exposure; rock is generally sound but looser than elsewhere on the route — test holds carefully.
Final short scramble/climbing moves to the true summit.
First rappel after traversing the summit ridge to the south-facing anchors.
Final rappel before navigating the crevasse field on the Chickamin Glacier back to camp.
